title: Farik Command
description: A request for the daemon to change something. Shaped like an event: command names what is asked and body carries that command's arguments. The pairing of the two is checked by the reader, farik_protocol::command::command_from_value. A command carries no actor: who asked is the session the command arrived on, and the step that turns a command into an event takes the actor from there rather than from the caller's word for it.

commandBodyWire.title: Command Body Wire
commandBodyWire.description: Every body shape a command carries. The branches have distinct required properties and none accepts an unknown one, so a body matches exactly one; contract_lock, contract_unlock, and task_integrate share taskIdBody for that reason. Which one a command must carry is decided by command, in the reader.

contract.description: A task contract. This schema says only that it is an object: one schema never references another, and the contract's rules, the repeated-id ones among them, belong to farik_core::contract::validate_contract, which the reader calls.

taskTransitionBody.title: Task Transition Body
taskTransitionBody.description: The human moves a task (docs/SPEC.md section 5.2) from any status but escalated. reason is recorded on the move; from blocked it is also the blocker's resolution, and into escalated it is the escalation's words.

humanAcceptBody.title: Human Accept Body
humanAcceptBody.description: The human approves a contract awaiting approval, or accepts a result that waits for them (docs/SPEC.md sections 5.4 and 5.16). An epic's result needs a message, which the reader's caller holds it to.

escalationResolveBody.title: Escalation Resolve Body
escalationResolveBody.description: The human resolves an escalation (docs/SPEC.md section 5.7) by moving the task to a status, with a message the next session about it is given.

questionAnswerBody.title: Question Answer Body
questionAnswerBody.description: The human answers a question an agent asked (docs/SPEC.md section 5.7): question_id is the sequence number of its question.asked.

taskIdBody.title: Task Id Body
taskIdBody.description: The body of a command that names one task and nothing else: contract_lock, contract_unlock, and task_integrate.

agentUpdateBody.title: Agent Update Body
agentUpdateBody.description: The human changes an agent's status (docs/SPEC.md F1). Only the status in phase 3; phase 5's team builder widens it.

sessionStopBody.title: Session Stop Body
sessionStopBody.description: The human stops a running session (docs/SPEC.md section 5.2).

sprintStartBody.title: Sprint Start Body
sprintStartBody.description: The human starts a sprint (docs/SPEC.md sections 3 and 5.5): what it may spend, or null for no budget of its own (ADR 0015). budget_usd is required so that this body matches no other branch.

emptyBody.title: Empty Body
emptyBody.description: The body of a command that carries nothing: run_stop and sprint_end.

commandReply.title: Command Reply
commandReply.description: What the daemon's POST /command answers once the token passes (docs/SPEC.md section 8.2): what the command did, as one sentence and the sequence numbers of the events it appended, or why it did nothing. A reply is what leaves a process, so it has a schema as a command does; farik_protocol::command::reply_from_value reads it against this definition.

kind.description: invalid: the command cannot be handled as given, a schema refusal among them; refused: it cannot be done to what it names as things stand; not_found: what it names is not there; failed: the store, a file, git, or the orchestrator failed.

taskStatus.title: Task Status
taskStatus.description: Where a contract is in the lifecycle of docs/SPEC.md section 5.2, the contract schema's own list.
